summary: The [Plan Strategique Numerique 2023-2028](2025-08-04 Madagascar - Digital Economy (Country Commercial Guide)) is the standing national digital strategy, with no published implementation report held.
developments:
The plan is recorded as in force and is the country's only whole-of-government digital instrument on file ([plan](2025-08-04 Madagascar - Digital Economy (Country Commercial Guide))).

No implementation report, mid-term review or costing under it has been published, and the projects recorded elsewhere in this ledger cite donor programmes rather than the plan as their authority.

summary: Three of four known open-data platforms were reachable in August 2026 and [no whole-of-government open-data policy or mandate](2026-08-09-madagascar-assemblee-nationale-open-data-api) is held.
developments:
A capture of August 2026 confirms institution-specific resources rather than a national programme: a licensed parliamentary open-data interface, a gated national-statistics microdata platform and an unconfirmed general portal ([capture](2026-08-09-madagascar-assemblee-nationale-open-data-api), [microdata](2026-08-09-madagascar-instat-microdata-platform), [portal](2026-08-09-madagascar-opendata-mg-portal)).

The finance ministry's own portal does not resolve. No open-data policy, public-sector information reuse instrument or publication mandate is held for the country.

summary: The [data-protection law of 2014](2025-02-25-gouvernance-numerique-donnees-personnelles-cmil-lexpress) has been in force since January 2015 and is recorded as unenforced.
developments:
The law is in force and unenforced, and excludes part of journalistic practice from its scope ([law](2025-02-25-gouvernance-numerique-donnees-personnelles-cmil-lexpress)).

Eleven years on, no amendment, implementing decree, enforcement action or guidance under it is held, and the supervisory body it provides for has never been constituted.

summary: A [complete recasting of the 2014 cybercrime law](2026-07-09-cybercriminalite-projet-loi-adopte-agenceecofin) is one of [three digital bills](2026-08-24-madagascar-extraordinary-session-electronic-communications-bill) before the extraordinary session opened on 25 August 2026.
developments:
The cybercrime bill reached the National Assembly carrying prison terms of two to ten years and providing for a new digital protection and investigation unit ([report](2026-08-31-tiatanindrazana-madagascar-cybercrime-bill-tabled)), presented as an update of the state's arsenal against rising digital risk ([account](2026-09-01-wearetech-madagascar-actualise-son-arsenal-face-a-la-montee)).

The bill was adopted by the Council of Ministers and would define security incidents and critical infrastructure organisations, revise electronic evidence and connection-data retention, and require operator cooperation with justice ([adoption](2026-07-09-cybercriminalite-projet-loi-adopte-agenceecofin), [account](2026-06-25-madagascar-new-cybersecurity-law-wearetech)).

Revision was reported again in August 2026 alongside signature of the United Nations cybercrime convention, with findings that artificial-intelligence-enabled fraud is outpacing African states' response capacity given as the reason ([revision](2026-08-15-madagascar-cybercrime-law-revision-ai-cooperation)).

Three of the seven bills on the session's order paper are digital: one on electronic communication and digital infrastructure, one recasting the cybercrime law and one authorising ratification of the convention ([order paper](2026-08-24-madagascar-extraordinary-session-electronic-communications-bill)). No bill texts are on file.

summary: A [draft electronic-signature and interoperability decree](2025-09-13-signature-electronique-interoperabilite-cadre-juridique-newsmada) was validated at a ministry workshop in September 2025 and has not been adopted.
developments:
The 2015 electronic-signature law has had no implementing decree; the draft validated in September 2025 would supply one and provides for a national interoperability committee ([draft](2025-09-13-signature-electronique-interoperabilite-cadre-juridique-newsmada)).

The minister named the recasting as a contribution to a future digital code, which is not held. A year on, no adoption, gazette reference or committee appointment is recorded.

summary: The [data-protection commission](2025-02-25-gouvernance-numerique-donnees-personnelles-cmil-lexpress) is provided for by the 2014 law and has never been constituted, its creation urged by an assessment mission in 2025.
developments:
The commission exists in the statute and not in fact, and an assessment mission urged its creation in February 2025 ([assessment](2025-02-25-gouvernance-numerique-donnees-personnelles-cmil-lexpress)).

No later account is held: no appointment, budget line, premises or supervisory decision, which is why the data-protection law beside it is recorded as unenforced rather than as breached.

summary: Madagascar took a citizen-facing administration position to the regional public service assembly ([report](2026-08-31-moov-madagascar-a-lassemblee-generale-annuelle-de-la-fonction)).
developments:
Madagascar argued at the regional public service annual general assembly for an administration turned towards citizens ([report](2026-08-31-moov-madagascar-a-lassemblee-generale-annuelle-de-la-fonction)).

Accession to the China-initiated network was approved by the Council of Ministers on 4 August 2026, mobilising the foreign affairs, justice, public-security, digital-development and gendarmerie ministries for cross-border cooperation on online fraud; no founding text, membership list, data-sharing rule or safeguard on what is exchanged is held ([accession](2026-08-10-madagascar-china-cybercrime-network-council-ministers), [editorial](2026-08-13-madagascar-online-scam-editorial-digital-trust)).

Signature of the United Nations convention is reported rather than evidenced by a depositary record, with no ratification instrument or parliamentary submission on record ([signature](2026-08-15-madagascar-cybercrime-law-revision-ai-cooperation)).

Membership of the world artificial-intelligence cooperation body was reported the same week, with no accession instrument, obligation or contribution held ([membership](2026-08-15-madagascar-cybercrime-law-revision-ai-cooperation)).

summary: The largest mobile money platform is documented as [conforming to the industry open interface standard](2025-03-31 MVola Madagascar - A case study for the GSMA Mobile Money API and open platforms), which is the only standards conformance on file.
developments:
The platform was documented as conformant in a March 2025 case study of the industry body's mobile money interface and open platforms ([case study](2025-03-31 MVola Madagascar - A case study for the GSMA Mobile Money API and open platforms)).

No national standards body, certification scheme or conformity register for digital systems is held, so the one standard the country demonstrably meets is a private-sector one adopted by a single operator.

progress: Regressed, a cabinet blocking order in force with no appeal route and a speech law announced beside it
summary: The cabinet [ordered pornographic sites blocked](2026-07-29-madagascar-blocks-obscene-content-sites) at provider level in July 2026, and a [dedicated social-media law](2026-07-29-madagascar-blocks-obscene-content-sites) covering defamation and disinformation was announced.
developments:
The Council of Ministers decided the blocking on 8 July 2026 on public-order grounds; it is in force as a cabinet decision with no timetable, technical mechanism, named regulator or appeal route specified ([order](2026-07-29-madagascar-blocks-obscene-content-sites)).

The communication minister announced a dedicated social-media law covering harassment, defamation and disinformation, with no draft held ([announcement](2026-07-29-madagascar-blocks-obscene-content-sites)). The base holds no civil-society or parliamentary record on digital governance against which to set either, which is itself the state of the debate.

summary: Two large programmes carry the digital agenda: a [US$143m governance and identification project](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin) that closed in June 2026 and a [US$375m connectivity project](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025) of which US$135m is digital.
developments:
The governance and identification project committed US$143,000,000 and closed on 30 June 2026 with the identity component continuing ([project](2020-09-29-wb-mdg-002-digital-governance-and-identification-management-system), [review](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin)).

The connectivity project's supervision record puts the envelope at US$375m, of which US$135m is digital, against a board approval of US$400,000,000 in March 2023 that a 2024 restructuring partly cancelled ([supervision](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025), [approval](2023-03-30-wb-mdg-001-digital-and-energy-connectivity-for-inclusion)).

A financial inclusion project was committed and restructured in October 2021 with no later implementation record ([restructuring](2021-10-13 Madagascar Financial Inclusion Project - Restructuring Paper (P161491, World Bank))), and a governance digitisation project was committed in 2021 with none either ([governance project](2021-01-01-afdb-mdg-001-madagascar---project-to-strengthen-governance)).

summary: The only non-state commitment on file is a [US$5.13m guarantee](2022-01-01-miga-mdg-airtel-mobile-money-2022-airtel-mobile-money-madagascar-digital-financial) to a mobile money business, committed in 2022 with no implementation record.
developments:
The guarantee of US$5,130,000 was committed in 2022 and no implementation record is held ([guarantee](2022-01-01-miga-mdg-airtel-mobile-money-2022-airtel-mobile-money-madagascar-digital-financial)).

No domestic venture fund, private placement or corporate investment in the country's digital sector is recorded, so the private half of the financing picture is one instrument four years old.

summary: A [5G-Advanced trial](2026-07-25-lexpress-mg-5g-advanced-yas-huawei-ministre) ran in July 2026 with no commercial 5G on record, above a [4G and 5G expansion programme](2025-04-11-eib-100m-axian-telecom-4g-5g-techafricanews) funded at US$100m.
developments:
The trial ran at an operator campus on 23 July 2026; the operator claims to be the fourth in the world to test the technology, and the claim is its own ([trial](2026-07-25-lexpress-mg-5g-advanced-yas-huawei-ministre), [account](2026-07-27-madagascar-5-5g-pilot-yas-madagascar)).

A development bank lent US$100m to the operator group under a European connectivity programme, US$40m of it for Madagascar, alongside US$82m of the group's own investment ([loan](2025-04-11-eib-100m-axian-telecom-4g-5g-techafricanews)); no coverage or site figure has been published since ([loan](2025-04-11-eib-100m-axian-telecom-4g-5g-techafricanews), [investment](2025-04-01-axian-telecom-82m-4g-madagascar-comoros-tanzania-techafricanews)).

No subscriber count, penetration rate or coverage share for the country is held at all.

summary: Operators and the state [agreed in December 2025 to cut mobile internet prices gradually](2025-12-02-connectivite-baisse-tarifs-internet-lexpress), with excise relief conditioned on reinvestment in quality.
developments:
The agreement ended a standoff between the state and the operators ([agreement](2025-12-02-connectivite-baisse-tarifs-internet-lexpress)).

No price schedule, reduction figure or implementation date was published with it, and no tariff basket or affordability measure for the country is held, so the base records that prices were agreed to fall and cannot say from what or to what.

summary: A [558 km Antananarivo to Mahajanga backbone](2025-12-05-orange-fibre-tana-mahajanga-2424) entered service in December 2025, built in eight months by the country's third fibre operator.
developments:
The link was inaugurated in December 2025 after eight months' construction ([backbone](2025-12-05-orange-fibre-tana-mahajanga-2424)).

It is the base's only national fibre construction record. No route map, capacity figure, wholesale price or measure of the pre-existing backbone is held, so the addition can be recorded and the total cannot.

summary: A [subsea cable extension](2025-09-10-dare1-cable-extension-madagascar-2424) to Mahajanga and Toliara was announced in September 2025, with work from 2026 and service from 2028.
developments:
The extension runs on a leg of 3,200 to 3,500 km via Tanzania and Mozambique and is ready for service in 2028 ([extension](2025-09-10-dare1-cable-extension-madagascar-2424), [route](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-kenya-south-africa-connectingafrica)).

No capacity, landing-station or price figure is published, and the base holds no measure of the country's existing international bandwidth against which to set the addition.

summary: A [direct-to-cell satellite trial](2026-07-15-direct-to-cell-satellite-trial-telecomreviewafrica) ran in July 2026 on operator spectrum, a [low-earth-orbit rural partnership](2026-06-01-airtel-eutelsat-rural-broadband-techafricanews) deepened, and [ten enclaved zones](2025-03-20-starlink-decim-dix-zones-enclavees-2424) remain unconnected.
developments:
The first direct-to-cell trial ran at Sadabe on 11 July 2026 on an operator's spectrum, the third African country to do so, with commercial launch pending the regulator ([trial](2026-07-15-direct-to-cell-satellite-trial-telecomreviewafrica), [authorisation](2026-05-19-starlink-direct-to-cell-fcc-airtel-spaceinafrica)).

A separate low-earth-orbit rural broadband partnership was deepened in June 2026, with no rural site count or subscriber figure published ([partnership](2026-06-01-airtel-eutelsat-rural-broadband-techafricanews)).

An arrangement to connect ten enclaved zones under the connectivity project was discussed in March 2025 and nothing has been connected, with no site or date published ([zones](2025-03-20-starlink-decim-dix-zones-enclavees-2424)).

summary: [Two renewable-powered national data centres](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin) were confirmed in June 2026 as securing the identity system, with no commissioning date published.
developments:
Tenders opened in December 2025 for rehabilitation of the main data centre and the identity-card personalisation centre ([tenders](2025-12-22-prodigy-tenders-data-center-biometricupdate)).

The two centres were confirmed at a portfolio review in June 2026 as the facilities securing the identity system ([review](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin)). No capacity, commissioning date, operator or resilience arrangement is published, and no commercial data-centre capacity in the country is recorded at all.

summary: The only rural electrification commitment on file is [US$17.07m for solar mini-grids](2019-01-01-norfund-mdg-welight-minigrid-2019-welight-solar-mini-grid-and-rural-electrification), committed in 2019 with no implementation record.
developments:
The commitment of US$17,067,987 was made in 2019 and no implementation record is held ([commitment](2019-01-01-norfund-mdg-welight-minigrid-2019-welight-solar-mini-grid-and-rural-electrification)).

No connection count, electrification rate or grid-coverage figure is held for the country, which matters here because the connectivity programmes recorded elsewhere in this ledger pair digital and energy inclusion in one project.

summary: A [multisectoral national cybersecurity strategy](2025-12-15-cybersecurite-strategie-nationale-midi) was launched at a December 2025 workshop on a three-month delivery target, and no document has been published.
developments:
The strategy was launched with a three-month delivery target and financed through the governance and identification programme; members of parliament flagged the 2014 cyber law as needing an update at the same workshop ([launch](2025-12-15-cybersecurite-strategie-nationale-midi)).

Eight months past that target, no strategy document is published. The base holds no national response team, no incident count and no readiness assessment for the country.

summary: The [Rahaka interoperability platform](2026-04-29-guichet-unique-en-ligne-interoperabilite-rahaka-lexpress) went live in April 2026 across five institutions, built on X-Road and run by the digital governance unit.
developments:
National interoperability was launched in April 2026, with an online one-stop window announced alongside it; the platform is operational at the investment board, the social-security fund, the statistics institute, the justice ministry and the tax directorate ([launch](2026-04-29-guichet-unique-en-ligne-interoperabilite-rahaka-lexpress)).

Expansion of the platform had been put out to tender in August 2025 ([tender](2025-08-28 Madagascar seeks firm to expand digital interoperability platform)). No transaction volume, service catalogue or connection roadmap beyond those five bodies is published.

summary: The first adult enrolment phase [registered more than six million people](2026-07-27-lexpress-mg-identite-biometrique-six-millions) against a two-million target, on [2,500 kits across 1,729 centres](2026-04-21-madagascar-biometric-enrollment-laxton-biometricupdate).
developments:
A steering committee validated the proof of concept and released 2,500 kits across 1,729 centres operating six days a week ([kits](2026-04-21-madagascar-biometric-enrollment-laxton-biometricupdate)); the January pilot had enrolled about 130,000 people across 116 centres in 26 communes ([kits](2026-04-21-madagascar-biometric-enrollment-laxton-biometricupdate), [pilot](2026-01-24-reforme-enrolement-biometrique-lexpress), [enrolment](2026-03-16-etat-civil-enrolement-biometrique-national-lexpress)).

More than six million adults were enrolled in the April to June 2026 phase, against a two-million target, with a second phase in preparation ([phase](2026-07-27-lexpress-mg-identite-biometrique-six-millions), [identity](2026-07-01-no-longer-invisible-legal-identity-worldbank)).

The counts are reported on different scopes and dates, from 2.6m in two months to over 5.6m in total ([counts](2026-06-05-madagascar-2-6m-digital-id-enrollments-biometricupdate), [review](2026-06-24-population-enregistrement-biometrique-5m-lexpress)), and no cost figure for either phase is reported. The pilot ran through regime change, civil unrest and a cyclone.

summary: A [law of 28 May 2026](2026-07-06-last-mile-civil-registration-biometricupdate) lets births be registered en masse inside the biometric enrolment operation, against a de-duplicated database.
developments:
Late birth registration had been available only through a costly judicial process; the new law permits mass registration within enrolment, with over 2,000 teams and more than 19,000 local chiefs confirming identities against a de-duplicated database ([law](2026-07-06-last-mile-civil-registration-biometricupdate)).

About six million adults, roughly 40 per cent, lacked a birth certificate ([identity](2026-07-01-no-longer-invisible-legal-identity-worldbank)), so the interoperability here is not a technical link between two working registers but the use of one operation to populate both at once.

summary: A [vendor was selected](2025-10-29-ecurrency-dsc3-eariary-cbdc-partner-prnewswire) in October 2025 for the central bank digital currency pilot, with the bank sole issuer and distribution private; no live pilot is reported.
developments:
Testing had been announced in May 2025 with no vendor named ([testing](2025-05-28 Madagascar Tests e-Ariary, Its Central Bank Digital Currency, to Modernize Payments)).

A platform was selected in October 2025 on a model where the central bank is sole issuer and distribution is private, and no live pilot has been reported since ([selection](2025-10-29-ecurrency-dsc3-eariary-cbdc-partner-prnewswire)). No other supervisory act, licensing decision or payment-system rule of the central bank is held in this base.

summary: A [digital-bank strategy](2025-11-26-axian-digibank-fintech-rebrand-techcabal) serving about 500,000 merchants a month was announced in November 2025, alongside a [business transactions application](2025-03-19 Madagascar - Orange Launches Mobile App (Orange Money Pro) for Business Transactions).
developments:
The fintech cluster was rebranded in November 2025 and its mobile money and payment products are being evolved toward a full digital bank across five markets, serving about 500,000 merchants a month ([strategy](2025-11-26-axian-digibank-fintech-rebrand-techcabal)).

A competing operator launched a business transactions application in March 2025, still in service with no take-up figures published ([application](2025-03-19 Madagascar - Orange Launches Mobile App (Orange Money Pro) for Business Transactions)). No government-to-business or business-to-government payment stream is separately recorded.

summary: A [bank was integrated into a mobile money service](2026-07-17-airtel-money-baobab-bank-partnership-techafricanews) in July 2026, giving bidirectional wallet-to-account transfers over short code and application.
developments:
The integration gives bidirectional transfers between wallet and bank account over unstructured supplementary service data and the bank's own application ([integration](2026-07-17-airtel-money-baobab-bank-partnership-techafricanews)).

It is the base's only record of a wallet and a bank interoperating in the country. No transfer volume, fee or count of participating banks is published.

progress: Mixed, active users at about a fifth of the population while the largest platform's core migration disrupted service
summary: [Six to seven million active mobile money users](2026-08-03-mvola-director-general-interview-trust-financial-inclusion) are reported against a population of about thirty million, and the [largest platform](2026-08-03-mvola-director-general-interview-trust-financial-inclusion) migrated its core with outages.
developments:
The active-user range is the operator's figure for the whole market, and it is not comparable with a 73 per cent usage figure in a 2025 study that measured awareness and use rather than active accounts ([users](2026-08-03-mvola-director-general-interview-trust-financial-inclusion)).

The largest platform replaced its core in May 2026, with outages and balance-display faults through May and June that the operator states were regularised ([migration](2026-08-03-mvola-director-general-interview-trust-financial-inclusion)). The account is the operator's alone, given three months after the fact: no regulator is named, no incident report is published and no compensation is mentioned.

summary: About [ten million civil records](2026-05-08-studia-ai-digitisation-civil-records-intelligentcio) were digitised across 1,695 communes, under an [EUR 8.5m registry and database contract](2025-05-16-madagascar-selects-in-groupe-8-5m-digital-id-biometricupdate) awarded in May 2025.
developments:
The digitisation covered about ten million records across 1,695 communes using optical character recognition and machine indexing, carried out with mobile satellite and solar units ([digitisation](2026-05-08-studia-ai-digitisation-civil-records-intelligentcio)).

A civil registry and database management contract of EUR 8.5m was awarded in May 2025, with no delivery milestone published since ([contract](2025-05-16-madagascar-selects-in-groupe-8-5m-digital-id-biometricupdate)). No completeness rate, error rate or count of records still on paper is held.

summary: A [full reconstitution of the electoral roll](2026-07-29-madagascar-ceni-full-electoral-roll-revision-2027) opened in July 2026, running four months and gated on presentation of a national identity card.
developments:
The reconstitution began at Talata Volonondry and runs to 24 November 2026 through five registration channels, replacing a roll the commission records as contested ([reconstitution](2026-07-29-madagascar-ceni-full-electoral-roll-revision-2027)).

The commission states that an unregistered citizen may not observe polling in their own place of residence, lodge a complaint or contest results, which makes the identity-card gate a condition on political participation and not only on voting.

summary: A [higher-education accreditation platform](2026-08-04-enseignement-superieur-la-plateforme-habilitation-accreditation-et-equivalence) entered service in 2026 and had taken 546 applications by 10 July.
developments:
The platform was presented at the ministry on 3 August 2026, having received 546 applications as at 10 July, of which about 250 were expected at the session opening on 21 September 2026 ([platform](2026-08-04-enseignement-superieur-la-plateforme-habilitation-accreditation-et-equivalence)).

It handles accreditation, authorisation and equivalence for higher-education programmes. No wider education management information system, enrolment database or school census platform is held for the country.

summary: A [police reporting platform](2026-07-30-madagascar-police-digital-platform-gbv-disappearances) for violence and disappearances entered service in July 2026, with anonymous filing and a citizen-visible reference number.
developments:
The platform runs around the clock on web and an Android application in Malagasy and French, allowing anonymous filing and giving the complainant a reference number they can see ([platform](2026-07-30-madagascar-police-digital-platform-gbv-disappearances), [account](2026-07-29-madagascar-la-police-nationale-numerise-le-signalement-des-violences)).

It was built by the national police's own information-systems directorate. No data controller, retention rule, deletion route or supervisory authority is named, which is the more serious gap on a system taking reports of gender-based violence.

summary: A [maritime single window](2026-08-07-madagascar-maritime-single-window-indonesia-financing) centralising port procedures is being deployed on Indonesian financing of about 816m ariary.
developments:
The financing was confirmed in August 2026 at more than 3.4bn Indonesian rupiah, about 816m ariary, through the port, maritime and river agency, and announced at the launch of a bilateral cooperation programme ([financing](2026-08-07-madagascar-maritime-single-window-indonesia-financing), [programme](2026-07-27-indo-aid-mdg-2026-maritime-single-window)).

No go-live date, port coverage, operator or procedure list is stated, so the base records a funded platform and nothing about what it will replace.

summary: The social-protection fund [put a human-resources management system out to tender](2026-08-12-madagascar-fid-erp-hr-software-recruitment) in August 2026, with bids due on 26 August.
developments:
The fund is recruiting a consultancy to build the system under a safety nets and resilience project, and separately tendered for a payroll server under a contingent emergency response project a week earlier ([tender](2026-08-12-madagascar-fid-erp-hr-software-recruitment)).

No contract value, scope or delivery date is disclosed. The two tenders are the only social-protection systems work on file, and both concern the fund's own administration rather than beneficiary management.

summary: An operator group was named a [founding partner of an African-language artificial-intelligence partnership](2026-07-28-axian-telecom-atlas-umoja-ai-malagasy-language) in July 2026, with no Malagasy model or dataset released.
developments:
The founding partnership was announced in July 2026 ([partnership](2026-07-28-axian-telecom-atlas-umoja-ai-malagasy-language)).

No Malagasy-language model, corpus or dataset has been released under it, and the country holds no national artificial-intelligence strategy against which the work could be set.

summary: A [customs data and artificial-intelligence centre](2025-06-07-douanes-madagascar-modele-ia-cedia-midi) has operated since May 2025 with a risk-targeting system and a data warehouse.
developments:
The centre was launched within the customs administration in May 2025 and operates an enhanced risk-assessment targeting system and a data warehouse; a multilateral institution selected the administration as its African pilot for artificial intelligence in customs operations that year ([centre](2025-06-07-douanes-madagascar-modele-ia-cedia-midi)).

No later account or performance figure is held, so the base records the most advanced sectoral use of the technology in the country and nothing about what it has caught or changed.

summary: A [partnership with Egypt on artificial intelligence in public administration](2026-08-01-madagascar-mndpt-youth-recruitment-digital-transformation) was reported in August 2026, with no signature date, text or figure.
developments:
The partnership was reported by the press with no date of signature given ([report](2026-08-01-madagascar-mndpt-youth-recruitment-digital-transformation)).

No text, figure or workstream is held, and no artificial-intelligence system is recorded in use in the country's general administration, so the record here is an intention and the working uses sit in customs instead.

progress: No change, a single indexed position with nothing earlier behind it
summary: The country was [placed behind regional comparators](2025-12-22-entrepreneuriat-digital-madagascar-retrait-lexpress) on a 2025 index of the digital entrepreneurship environment, reported at second hand.
developments:
The placement was reported through a development agency in December 2025, on an index the base holds only at second hand and carries as a dated citation rather than as current state ([index](2025-12-22-entrepreneuriat-digital-madagascar-retrait-lexpress)).

No count of firms, funding raised, incubator or accelerator is held for the country, so the position is the whole of the evidence and its components are not visible.

summary: A [technical assistance facility](2026-07-23-madagascar-facilite-assistance-technique-refondation-undp) running 2026 to 2030 had certified 170 focal points across the administration by the end of July 2026.
developments:
The facility was launched in July 2026 with development-programme support, and by the end of that month 170 focal points had been certified and proposals were being submitted through a dedicated platform ([facility](2026-07-23-madagascar-facilite-assistance-technique-refondation-undp), [account](2026-07-21-madagascar-fat-numerique)).

Interventions selected by its steering committee run three to nine months. No curriculum, completion rate or measure of what the certification covers is published.

summary: A [US$15m skills sub-component](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025) covers a virtual university, advanced skills training for 5,700 people and the national research network.
developments:
The sub-component commits US$15m, with 5,700 people to be trained in advanced digital skills and US$2.4m for the national research network ([sub-component](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025)).

The figures are targets in a supervision record rather than outturns: no enrolment, completion or graduation count is held, and the virtual university is not recorded as opened.

summary: The ministry received [259 applications for ten established specialist posts](2026-08-01-madagascar-mndpt-youth-recruitment-digital-transformation) in artificial intelligence, data, cybersecurity, telecommunications and digital law.
developments:
The applications were received by 1 August 2026 for ten established civil-service posts, and no appointment has been announced ([recruitment](2026-08-01-madagascar-mndpt-youth-recruitment-digital-transformation)).

Applicants have publicly asked for integrity guarantees on the selection. The ratio is the only labour-market signal in the base for the country: no graduate count, employment figure or salary measure for the sector is held.

summary: A [university connectivity and artificial-intelligence initiative](2026-01-26-unipod-internet-ai-universities-techafricanews) was announced in January 2026, with no campus connected or facility opened on record.
developments:
The initiative would bring high-speed internet and artificial intelligence to universities ([initiative](2026-01-26-unipod-internet-ai-universities-techafricanews)).

Nothing has been recorded delivered under it since. No university department, research centre or think tank is recorded contributing to national digital policy, so the academic side of the record is an announcement and a funded skills line elsewhere in this ledger.

summary: An [affordable-device facility](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025) approved nine applications and made a US$2.5m first call, and [664,000 devices](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin) had been distributed by June 2026.
developments:
The facility is a US$24m sub-component of the connectivity project: an April 2025 call closed with nothing contracted, and by November 2025 nine applications were approved with only two operator contracts unsigned, a US$2.5m first call for funds made on 7 November and a student-laptop pilot proposed for about 700 computers ([facility](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025)).

The June 2026 portfolio review records 664,000 devices distributed, against a rural-connectivity tender document that slipped from October 2025 to January 2026 ([review](2026-06-24-madagascar-worldbank-review-543m-prodigy-decim-ecofin), [supervision](2025-11-20-worldbank-decim-madagascar-supervision-digital-nov-2025)).

summary: The statistics institute runs a [registration-gated microdata platform](2026-08-09-madagascar-instat-microdata-platform) advertising census and household-survey microdata, with no documentation beyond the landing page.
developments:
The platform was captured in August 2026 advertising household surveys covering 2020 to 2022, an enterprise survey and third-census microdata ([platform](2026-08-09-madagascar-instat-microdata-platform)).

The datasets themselves sit behind account registration and were not retrieved, and no dataset documentation, sample size, licence or reuse terms are established beyond the landing page, so the base records that the microdata exists and not what is in it.

summary: The national assembly runs a [licensed open-data interface](2026-08-09-madagascar-assemblee-nationale-open-data-api) serving five parliamentary datasets, while a [general portal](2026-08-09-madagascar-opendata-mg-portal) carries no datasets or issuing institution.
developments:
The parliamentary interface serves deputies, legislative texts, sittings, committees and parliamentary groups as structured data under an open licence compatible with attribution reuse, rate-limited to 60 requests a minute; its page counters read 163 deputies, 45 texts and 128 sittings at capture ([interface](2026-08-09-madagascar-assemblee-nationale-open-data-api)).

The general portal is a reachable landing page with six undated category tiles and four unlinked project cards, naming no issuing institution, dataset count or licence, and its footer credits only a private vendor, so it is not established as a government portal ([portal](2026-08-09-madagascar-opendata-mg-portal)).

summary: A [telecommunications modernisation loan](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mdg-001-telecommunications-modernization-project) of RMB 337.9m sits behind the network, and the cabinet approved accession to a [China-initiated cybercrime network](2026-08-10-madagascar-china-cybercrime-network-council-ministers) in August 2026.
developments:
The concessional loan of RMB 337.9m, about US$54,708,617 at the capture conversion, was committed in 2020 with no implementation record held ([loan](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mdg-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-3379-million), [project](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-mdg-001-telecommunications-modernization-project)).

Accession to the cybercrime network was approved on 4 August 2026, mobilising five ministries and the gendarmerie for cross-border cooperation on online fraud ([accession](2026-08-10-madagascar-china-cybercrime-network-council-ministers)).

Those two instruments, a decade apart in kind, are the whole of the recorded relationship: no vendor contract, data centre or technology framework is separately held.

summary: Two public tenders opened for computing equipment and network build-out ([tender](2026-08-29-madagascar-fid-cerp-n87-materiels-informatiques)).
developments: The development intervention fund opened two tenders, one for computing equipment and one for the equipment to build a computer network ([tender](2026-08-29-madagascar-fid-cerp-n87-materiels-informatiques)). The tenders are open; no award, value or specification is on the base.
